items.description: Rulings page: one proposed rule plus an example per topic — stage naming, stage granularity, checkout, pod definition, secrets and `withVault` scope, timeouts, `post`/`notify`, file naming and headers, and when code goes into the library — in the slice folder. "Stage granularity and the library rule are judgment calls, so Claude doesn't settle them alone." The operator rules before the guide is written: the rulings stand in plan.md's Requirements / rulings before the first guide page is committed.
items.rationale: rulings.md in the slice folder; P4 r1-r3 reviews and consult_2 confirmed the rulings stand in plan.md before the first guide page commit (P5 paused for them).

items.description: A dedicated section on stage labels ("Please have a dedicated section for labeling stages. I find these very messy and all over the place."). It sits next to the section on stage granularity, not inside it.
items.rationale: docs/pages/guide/stage-labels.md is its own page beside stage-granularity.md, both in the guide nav; served from https://pipelines.home/docs/.

items.description: The cookbook — the style guide itself, strict ("I want it to be followed strictly"), with examples, covering every pipeline type: rules written as MUSTs with the reason for each, one complete reference Jenkinsfile per pipeline type of the inventory, a short recipe per topic, and declarative only (J08 is "migrate all").
items.rationale: Guide: 12 topic pages with MUST rules; 13 type pages + 14 complete example Jenkinsfiles; all declarative. Served live at pipelines.home/docs/ (llms-full.txt 196 KB).

items.description: "Every example passes the declarative linter": each example, an excerpt inside the complete file it is cut from, passes the controller's full check at `/pipeline-model-converter/validate`, and the published example is byte for byte the one checked.
items.rationale: lint_examples.py (docs lint GREEN in sweep r1) sends each example minus marker lines to /pipeline-model-converter/validate. Test phase: every non-blank line of all 14 examples found verbatim in the served llms-full.txt, so published text is what was linted.

items.area: R4 — The rulings the guide carries
items.description: The guide carries exactly the rulings of review plan §4 and the operator's rulings from the rulings page: J24 (`checkout scm` for the job's own repo), J23 (the one load line, floating on `main`, no pin), J01 (the job-properties block and its placement, in declarative `options {}`/`triggers {}`; retention is the global build discarder, so files declare none), J08 (declarative), J11/J12 (the standard timeout, and only the exceptions the rulings page settles, ruling F5; the iac files' 4-hour backstop with a `post { aborted }` notify), J17 (`withVault` scope), J19 (the iac dev-stage duplication is deliberate: those files stay self-contained), the §6a result (what a new repo needs for its push hook), non-secret settings inline rather than as global env vars (Q6; `HA_URL` is the ruled exception, and endpoints never go into OpenBao), `notify` use, `Jenkinsfile.*` naming, and header comments.
items.rationale: P5 r1/r2 code reviews and consult_2 checked each ruling (J24,J23,J01,J08,J11/12,J17,J19,§6a,Q6,notify,naming,headers) against the guide pages; sampled pages exist (checkout, job-properties, timeouts, secrets, post-and-notify, file-layout, new-repo, library). Content judged on reviews + page read, not re-derived line by line.

items.area: R4 — Stage generators and computed triggers
items.description: The guide has a recipe for each pipeline that generates stages or computes its triggers: `DockerImages/Jenkinsfile` (a stage per image variant), `Intercom/Jenkinsfile` (a stage pair per hardware version) and `Architecture/Jenkinsfile` (triggers computed from YAML, which `triggers {}` cannot express).
items.rationale: types/image-matrix, types/firmware (Intercom/firmware stage pairs) and types/architecture-collector (computed triggers) with examples image-matrix.groovy, firmware.groovy, architecture-collector.groovy, all linted.

items.area: R4 — The pod helper (033 close-out B3)
items.description: The guide describes the pod helper as it is — the global var `podYaml`, called as `podYaml(templates: [...], images: [...])` inside `agent { kubernetes { ... } }` — and states the map form of an `images:` entry with an explicit container `name:`.
items.rationale: guide/pod.md and reference/podYaml.md (vars/podYaml.md) describe podYaml(templates:, images:) in agent { kubernetes }, map form with name:; PodYamlTest extended (7 tests).
evidence: /work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/podYaml.groovy exists as its own var at d9ff168

items.area: R5 — When code goes into the library
items.description: When code goes into the library ("And when do we put something into the utility library."): the guide gives a decision test, with examples from the estate — J14/J15/J16 are accepted helpers, and J19 was ruled against ("Keep the duplication; the style guide says it is deliberate").
items.rationale: guide/library.md: decision test with J14/J15/J16 accepted and J19 ruled against (P5 review).

items.area: R6 — Docs site source and build
items.description: Docs site: source in `JenkinsPipelineUtils/docs/`, built with MkDocs + Material (ruling D2) on KubeCoder's manual as the basis, "including its LLM support": `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a per-page `.md` copy for every page, plus the validation settings under which the build fails `--strict` on an orphaned page, a missing target, an absolute link or a broken anchor. The strict build runs in the library's `kc project test`.
items.rationale: docs/mkdocs.yml: Material, llmstxt plugin (llms.txt, llms-full.txt, per-page .md), validation warn-keys under --strict; check_site.py in kc project test (docs test GREEN in sweep). Served llms.txt 200 and llms-full.txt 200.

items.description: "Hostname: pipelines.home/docs, with an index page at /." The site image serves a small landing page at `/` that links to the docs, and the docs under `/docs/`. The name is LAN-only, published by the Service annotations with a step-ca certificate, and the image's nginx config passes `nginx -t` at build time.
items.rationale: Live: https://pipelines.home/ serves the landing page (200, 1295 B), /docs/ 200, TLS trusted from this pod (step-ca); nginx -t at image build witnessed by P9. LAN-only via chart values (P8).

items.area: R6 / D6 — The site is live
items.description: Once the ArgoCDDeploy push lands, Argo syncs the `pipelines` app on its own, with no Argo action by anyone (ruling D6). `https://pipelines.home/` then answers with the landing page, and `https://pipelines.home/docs/` and its `llms.txt` answer with the guide, when fetched from a KubeCoder environment. The site is served from the image tag that the latest site build pinned in PipelinesDeploy.
items.rationale: Pushed ArgoCDDeploy a854420 with no Argo action by anyone; within ~1 minute https://pipelines.home/, /docs/, /docs/llms.txt all 200. Served files last-modified 19:52:11 = site build IaC/JenkinsPipelineUtils #1, whose pin 302b1a0 is on PipelinesDeploy main. Could not read the Application object (no kubectl in this container), so the served site is the evidence.

items.description: The site is served as its own small app, the way charts.home is served (ruling D1). The library's Jenkinsfile follows the guide, and a job created through the API runs it. Its first build from the pushed library is green: it pushes the site image to `registry:5000` and writes the image pin into PipelinesDeploy's prd values. The job builds and publishes the site only; slice 033's ruling that the library's tests get no Jenkins job stands.
items.rationale: Library push 973257a started IaC/JenkinsPipelineUtils #1 by the hook: SUCCESS, pushed image, pin commit 302b1a0 'ci: image pins from IaC/JenkinsPipelineUtils #1' on PipelinesDeploy main. Job config saved at xml/IaC/JenkinsPipelineUtils.xml. Library has no tests job.

items.area: R6 / D1 / D6 — Deploy repo and registrations
items.description: PipelinesDeploy is shaped like ChartsDeploy, and its `kc project test` is green, with the placeholder manifest replaced by the real one. `AaC/PipelinesDeploy`'s first build is green and archives the producer's artifact.
